composio.note: Kintone REST is listed under bring-your-own OAuth app in Composio docs, so create the auth config with your own client ID and secret.

need_own_app.answer: Yes. Composio has no managed OAuth app for Kintone REST, so you must register an OAuth client in Kintone and give Composio its client ID and secret.

Managed apps show Composio's name on consent and share quota
Custom scopes need your own app

scenarios.label: Agent acting on Kintone domains with OAuth
scenarios.when_this_applies: Each Kintone domain (yours or a customer's) has an admin register an OAuth client and enable users.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

waiting.basis: No provider review found in the docs (G2); review timelines not found.

scenarios.approval: No provider review found. Clients are registered by an admin in the Kintone Integration settings; each domain's admin must also enable users.

modifiers.note: Admin registers client and selects permitted users
IP-restricted domains must allowlist the client's IP

extras: Admin registers client and selects permitted users
IP-restricted domains must allowlist the client's IP

prerequisites.title: Admin access to a Kintone domain
prerequisites.detail: Clients are created under User & System Administration, then OAuth under System Administration.

prerequisites.title: Redirect URI from Composio
prerequisites.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and enter it as the required redirect endpoint.

steps.title: Open OAuth settings in Kintone
steps.detail: Log in as admin, open User & System Administration, then OAuth under System Administration.
steps.done_when: The OAuth client list is visible.

steps.title: Copy redirect URI from Composio
steps.detail: Get the callback URL from the Composio dashboard and check it is a clean URL.
steps.done_when: Redirect URI is ready to paste.

steps.title: Add the OAuth client
steps.detail: Click Add OAuth Client, enter a client name (required), optional logo, and the redirect endpoint, then save.
steps.done_when: Client ID and secret are generated.

steps.title: Enable users with Configure users
steps.detail: Check the users who may use the client. New users are unchecked by default.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the kintone_rest auth config via Composio's API with the client ID and secret, and requested scopes separated by spaces.

steps.title: Allowlist IPs if restricted
steps.detail: If the domain uses IP restrictions, ask the admin to allow the IP that runs the OAuth client.
steps.done_when: Connection works from the restricted domain.

traps.title: New users are disabled by default
traps.detail: Users cannot use the client until checked in Configure users, and each new Kintone user starts unchecked.

traps.title: IP restrictions block OAuth
traps.detail: OAuth client features fail on domains with IP restrictions unless the client's IP is allowlisted.

traps.title: Token and code lifetimes
traps.detail: Authorization codes last 10 minutes and access tokens 1 hour; refresh tokens do not expire. Up to 10 refresh tokens per client per user.

traps.title: Redirect URI must match exactly
traps.detail: The token request must use the same URL-encoded redirect value as the authorization request.

traps.title: Scopes cap the token
traps.detail: A token can only call APIs in its scope, and scopes never exceed the user's own access.

blockers.what_it_means: The user is not checked in Configure users.
blockers.what_to_do: Have the domain admin check the user in Configure users.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft instructions for the customer admin.

blockers.symptom: OAuth fails on a customer domain
blockers.what_it_means: The domain uses IP restrictions and your server IP is not allowed.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the customer admin to allowlist your server IP.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the request listing the IP.
